title: introduce-conditional-kms-grant-and-audit-fencework
author: Maya Liang
description: Motivation: Customers operating under regional compliance regimes need policy-driven, per-request KMS grants that are conditional on verified residency claims while producing tamper-evident audit material. This PR implements a conditional KMS grant flow and an "audit-fencework" that ensures audit messages include provenance and region-binding proofs. The feature is opt-in behind feature_flag.residency_conditional_kms and rolled out as a shadow path for 2 weeks before switching to active grants. What changed: 1) policy-compiler: new ConditionalKmsGrant rule type that evaluates residency assertions and operator-scoped attributes to mint ephemeral KMS grants via the kms-proxy; 2) kms-proxy: added grant issuance API that returns scoped, time-bound wrapping tokens and enforces region affinity with fallbacks; 3) audit-ingestor: added fencework envelope that attaches residency-proof-hash and kms-grant-id to each audit record and emits SHA256 chain anchors to the immutable-audit-store; 4) rbac-e2e tests: added test matrix covering tenant-scoped and operator-scoped requests, and negative tests for mismatched residency; 5) console: UI flag and rollout control for enabling conditional grants per-tenant; 6) docs: migration and security considerations. Compatibility: the flow falls back to existing static CMK usage if the policy or KMS endpoint returns errors; audit envelopes are always emitted to avoid telemetry gaps. Rollout plan: shadow enable on internal staging for 48 hours, limited customer beta with opt-in tenants for 2 weeks, then lift shadow to active for tenants with compliance profiles. Risk mitigations: rate-limit grant issuance, cache positive residency assertions for short TTL, and add metric rbac.conditional_kms_grants_error_rate for alerting. See linked Linear ENG-4728 and security ticket SEC-909 for threat model and customer ask.

release_notes: - Opt-in Conditional KMS Grants: Per-request ephemeral KMS grants conditioned on verified residency claims. Disabled by default; enable via feature_flag.residency_conditional_kms. - Audit Fencework: Audit records now carry residency-proof-hash and kms-grant-id anchors for non-repudiation and easier forensic queries. - Fallback: Safe fallback to static CMK on issuer failures to preserve availability. - Rollout: Beta for selected tenants; see docs/security/conditional_kms.md for migration and support instructions.
notes_for_ops: Ops: add alert rule if rbac.conditional_kms_grants_error_rate > 0.5% for 5m, and monitor rbac.conditional_kms_grant_latency P95. Ensure kms-proxy has permission to call tenant CMKs in tenant-account, and KMS quotas are sufficient during beta. If enabling for tenant, pre-warm residency cache by running attestation sweep script in docs.
security_considerations: Ephemeral grants are time-bound and scoped to wrapping-only usage; grants include a region affinity tag that is validated by kms-proxy. Audit envelopes intentionally avoid including tenant PII; residency-proof is a deterministic hash. Threat model reviewed in SEC-909; mitigations added including rate limiting, circuit-breaker, and explicit fallback to static CMK. Operator-scoped actions require an additional attribute 'operator:residency_affirmed' to prevent privilege escalation.
testing_matrix: Unit tests: policy compiler and kms-proxy logic; Integration: kms-proxy <-> KMS simulator with region mismatch scenarios; E2E: tenant-positive, tenant-negative, operator-scoped and forced-fallback scenarios; Performance: grant issuance QPS tested at 500 qps in staging with caching enabled. All tests included in CI and validated on staging during shadow run.
